speaker: Doctor
text: Welcome to my office. I understand you are experiencing dizziness, nausea, and imbalance; to help narrow this down, have these symptoms been constant or do they come in waves? Also, have you noticed any ringing in your ears or hearing loss?

speaker: Patient
text: 27-year-old male. The patient reports a sustained sensation of the room spinning since this morning, which is low grade and constant. He occasionally feels nauseous and has taken diphenhydramine to help him sleep, which also alleviates his symptoms slightly. He mentions recent increased intake of garlic due to trying to recover from a cold a few days ago. Past medical history is unremarkable.

speaker: Doctor
text: DIAGNOSIS READY: Vestibular Neuritis (likely viral etiology post-cold). The history of constant spinning vertigo lasting hours, nausea, and relief from antihistamines, without mention of hearing loss, strongly points to inflammation of the vestibular nerve rather than Meniere's disease.
